description: Enable/disable kernel auditing; change auditing filter rules; retrieve auditing status and filter rules. Required for `auditctl -e 1` and rule manipulation.
Write records to kernel auditing log. Granted to PAM-driven login programs that need to log session-start records.
Employ features that can block system suspend (epoll EPOLLWAKEUP, /proc/sys/wake_lock writes).

Use most BPF facilities (load programs, create maps). Split out from CAP_SYS_ADMIN in 5.8 to enable least-privilege BPF tooling. Note: tracing-class BPF still needs CAP_PERFMON; networking-class needs CAP_NET_ADMIN.
Read /proc/<pid>/{maps,statm,smaps,stack,syscall} of any process; bypass /proc/sys/kernel/{ns_last_pid,nstgid_last,etc.} restrictions; needed by CRIU. Split out from CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
Make arbitrary changes to file UIDs/GIDs (without it, only owner can chown to own group). Container `chown` inside images requires this; Docker grants by default.
Bypass file read/write/execute permission checks (DAC = discretionary access control). Effectively 'I am root for file access regardless of mode bits.'
Bypass file read and directory read+execute (search) permission checks. Weaker than CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE — read/list-only, no write.
Operations that normally require the file's UID to match the process EUID — chmod, chown of group, utimes on others' files, sticky-bit unlink override.
Don't clear setuid/setgid bits when modifying a file you don't own. Without it, write/chown of a setuid file as a non-owner clears the bit.
Lock memory (mlock, mlockall, mmap MAP_LOCKED, shmctl SHM_LOCK). Required by some real-time / crypto / DB workloads to keep secrets out of swap.
Bypass permission checks for System V IPC objects.
Bypass permission checks for sending signals (kill any process). Without it, only same-EUID/RUID and a few signals to children.
LSM-specific: SELinux/AppArmor admin operations (load policy, change enforcing mode).
Override MAC (mandatory access control) policy. Effective only on Smack LSM (and a few others); SELinux/AppArmor have their own bypass mechanisms.
Create special files (mknod for char/block devices). Container runtimes drop this by default — root inside a container can't create new device nodes.
Network admin: interface config, routing, firewall (iptables/nftables), netfilter, multicast, packet socket bind. Required to manipulate routes inside a container.
Bind a socket to privileged ports (<1024). The lowest-privilege way to run a non-root webserver on port 80/443.
Make socket broadcasts and listen to multicasts. Rarely needed; mostly historical.
Use RAW and PACKET sockets; bind to any address for transparent proxying. Required for ping (without setuid), tcpdump, traceroute. Container runtimes typically drop this.
Use performance monitoring (perf_event_open, full BPF tracing). Split from CAP_SYS_ADMIN in 5.8.
Make arbitrary GID manipulations (setgid, setresgid, setgroups). Forge GID in unix-domain socket credentials.
Set arbitrary file capabilities on files (extended attributes 'security.capability'). Required to install setcap-style bestowal.
Drop any capability from any process's bounding set; raise inheritable caps not in the calling thread's permitted set.
Make arbitrary UID manipulations (setuid, setreuid, setresuid, setfsuid). Forge UID in unix socket credentials.

The 'kitchen sink' capability — mount, swapon/swapoff, sethostname, namespace setup, BPF (pre-5.8), keyctl, ioperm/iopl, vm86, and many more. Often called 'the new root' because dropping it disables most container-relevant operations.
Use reboot(2) and kexec_load(2). Reboot the system.
chroot(2) the calling process and change mount namespaces via setns(2)+CLONE_NEWNS.
Load and unload kernel modules. Container runtimes always drop — letting a container load modules = compromised host.
Raise nice value, change scheduling policy/priority of any process, set IO scheduling class/priority, set CPU affinity beyond own.
Use acct(2) — process accounting on/off.

Trace any process (ptrace, /proc/<pid>/mem, perf_event_open with PERF_SAMPLE_REGS_USER, etc.). Required for gdb/strace on non-children. Yama LSM /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope=2 restricts further.
Perform IO port operations (iopl, ioperm); access /proc/kcore, /dev/mem, /dev/kmem; raw block-device IO (e.g. SG_IO ioctls).
Override resource limits — set RLIMIT_NPROC > current, override fs reserved-block disk-quota, override max user inotify watches, etc.
Set system clock (settimeofday, stime, adjtimex), set realtime hardware clock.
Read kernel logs (klogctl); change console log level. Required for `dmesg` when /proc/sys/kernel/dmesg_restrict=1.
Trigger system wake from suspend (CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM, CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM timers).
Set FS_APPEND_FL and FS_IMMUTABLE_FL inode flags via chattr.
Establish leases on arbitrary files via fcntl F_SETLEASE.
Use vhangup(2). TTY config tweaks like KDFONTOP ioctl.
Create new user namespace. Initially: child has full caps inside, no caps outside. Allows unprivileged container creation.
Create new PID namespace. First process becomes pid 1 of the namespace.
Create new mount namespace (named NEWNS for historical 'new namespace' meaning, when there was only one type).
Create new IPC namespace (System V IPC, POSIX message queues).
Create new UTS namespace (hostname, domainname).
Create new network namespace.
Create new cgroup namespace. Virtualizes /proc/self/cgroup view.
Create new time namespace (CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_BOOTTIME offsets). Kernel 5.6+. NOTE: Cannot be passed to unshare(2)/clone(2) — set via /proc/<pid>/ns/time_for_children + setns.
Share virtual memory with parent. Used by pthread_create. Without CLONE_VM, fork-style copy-on-write.
Share filesystem state (root, cwd, umask). Required by pthreads.
Share file descriptor table. Used by pthreads (so threads share open FDs).
Share signal handlers. Required when CLONE_THREAD is set.
Place child in same thread group as parent. Requires CLONE_SIGHAND. Requires CLONE_VM in modern kernels. Foundation of pthread_create.
Make parent of new child the same as parent of caller (sibling instead of child). SIGCHLD goes to grandparent.
Return a pidfd referring to the child via the parent_tidptr arg. Race-free signaling via pidfd_send_signal.
Share IO context with parent (CFQ scheduler grouping).
Historical flag; ignored in modern kernels. Documented for completeness.
Tracer cannot force CLONE_PTRACE on this clone. Used by kernel threads.
Store child TID in parent_tidptr in the parent's memory.
Store child TID in child_tidptr in the child's memory.
Clear child_tidptr on child exit and futex-wake any waiter — the mechanism behind pthread_join.
Hard memory ceiling for the cgroup. Allocations beyond trigger reclaim then OOM kill (within cgroup). The systemd `MemoryMax=` directive writes here.
Throttle threshold — kernel aggressively reclaims when usage exceeds. No OOM (unlike .max). systemd `MemoryHigh=`.
Soft protection — usage below this is preferred over reclaim from sibling cgroups. Best-effort. systemd `MemoryLow=`.
Hard protection — kernel will not reclaim below this. Stronger guarantee than memory.low. systemd `MemoryMin=`.
Current memory usage of the cgroup including all descendants.
Lines: low, high, max, oom, oom_kill counts. Watching this is how systemd-oomd reacts before global OOM.
Swap ceiling for the cgroup. 0 disables swap usage by this cgroup. systemd `MemorySwapMax=`.
PSI metric for memory contention. Lines: 'some avg10=… avg60=… avg300=… total=…' and 'full ...'. The data behind oomd.
CFS quota+period for the cgroup. e.g. '50000 100000' = 50% of one CPU. systemd `CPUQuota=`.
Relative CPU share weight under contention. Higher = more CPU. systemd `CPUWeight=` (mapped from a 1-10000 scale; default 100).
Per-cgroup CPU accounting: usage_usec, user_usec, system_usec, nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_usec. Throttling diagnostic.
PSI for CPU contention.
Per-device IO bandwidth/IOPS ceiling. e.g. '8:0 rbps=1048576 wbps=1048576 riops=100 wiops=100'. systemd `IOMax*=`.
Relative IO share. systemd `IOWeight=`.
Per-device 'rbytes wbytes rios wios dbytes dios'. Block-layer IO; doesn't include pagecache hits.
PSI for IO contention.
Hard ceiling on number of processes/threads in the cgroup. Hitting it causes fork()/clone() to fail with EAGAIN. systemd `TasksMax=`.
Current process count in cgroup including descendants.
Members of the cgroup. Write a PID to add a process (and all its threads); read to enumerate. The way to move a process between cgroups.
Per-thread membership (only in 'threaded' cgroups).
Controllers available in this cgroup (filtered by parent's subtree_control).
Controllers enabled for direct child cgroups. Write '+memory' / '-cpu' to add/remove. Cannot enable a controller in a cgroup that has processes (no-internal-procs rule).
populated (1 if any descendant has procs), frozen (1 if cgroup.freeze took effect). poll/epoll friendly.
Write 1 to freeze every process in cgroup atomically; 0 to thaw.
Write 1 to SIGKILL every process in cgroup. v5.14+. Cleaner alternative to walking cgroup.procs.
Cgroup type. 'domain' = standard process-grouping. 'threaded' = thread-grouping mode for fine-grained scheduling.
CPUs the cgroup may run on. Hard pin. systemd `AllowedCPUs=`.
Memory NUMA nodes allowed.
If 1, OOM kill in this cgroup kills every process in it atomically (vs single-victim default).
v1 cpuset controller — CPUs the cgroup runs on.
v1 cpuset — NUMA memory nodes allowed.
v1 memory hard limit.
v1 memory soft limit (best-effort).
v1 per-cgroup swappiness override.
v1 OOM control: write 'oom_kill_disable 1' to suspend processes instead of killing on OOM.
v1 relative CPU weight. v2 equivalent: cpu.weight.
v1 CFS quota per period.
v1 CFS period.
v1 RT scheduling runtime per period.
v1 block IO relative weight.
v1 read bandwidth ceiling per device.
v1 write bandwidth ceiling per device.
v1 device allowlist entry. Type a/b/c (any/block/char). e.g. 'c 1:3 rmw' = char dev 1:3 read/mknod/write.
v1 device denylist entry. Same format as devices.allow.
v1 freezer controller state. Replaced by cgroup.freeze in v2.
v1 pids controller — process count ceiling.
Kill the process (entire thread group). The 'never recover' verdict.
Kill only the offending thread. Older 'KILL' alias maps here.
Send SIGSYS to the thread; siginfo.si_call_addr/si_syscall set.
Return the configured errno value to userspace without executing the syscall.
Suspend the thread and forward the syscall to a userspace supervisor over a notification FD.
If a ptracer is attached, notify it (PTRACE_EVENT_SECCOMP). Otherwise return ENOSYS.
Allow the syscall but log it (audit).
Allow the syscall (the default for unmatched).
Set the calling thread's name (max 16 chars). Visible in /proc/<pid>/comm and ps -L.
Set signal to receive when parent dies. Cleared on setuid execve.
Set the per-thread no_new_privs bit (one-way; cleared only by exit/exec). Required for unprivileged seccomp filter installation.
Set seccomp mode (1=strict, 2=filter). For filter mode, requires no_new_privs OR CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
Preserve permitted capabilities across UID 0→nonzero transitions. Cleared on execve.
Drop a capability from the bounding set. One-way.
Test if a capability is in the bounding set.
Manipulate ambient capability set: PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE / LOWER / IS_SET / CLEAR_ALL sub-ops.
Mark calling thread as subreaper for orphaned descendants.
Set securebits flags (NOROOT, NO_SETUID_FIXUP, KEEP_CAPS, plus *_LOCKED counterparts).
Control whether the process is dumpable (core dump allowed; ptrace attach allowed). Reset on setuid execve to 'suid_dumpable' value.
Auto-restart certain blocking syscalls interrupted by signal (instead of returning EINTR). Doesn't help all syscalls — read/write/wait yes; sleep/poll no.
Use 3-arg sa_sigaction handler (signo, siginfo_t*, ucontext_t*) instead of legacy sa_handler. Required to access fault address, sender PID, etc.
For SIGCHLD: don't deliver when child is stopped/continued (only on exit).
For SIGCHLD: auto-reap children — they don't become zombies. The 'lazy' alternative to wait().
Don't add this signal to the mask while handler runs (allows reentry).
Reset disposition to SIG_DFL after first delivery (System V signal() semantics).
Run handler on alternate signal stack (set up via sigaltstack(2)). Useful for SIGSEGV handlers when main stack overflows.
Read-only mount. Equivalent to mount -o ro.
setuid/setgid bits ignored on this mount. Common on /home, /tmp, container rootfs to limit privilege escalation surface.
Disallow access to device special files. Container runtimes apply on every non-/dev mount.
Disallow executing programs from this mount. Hardening for /tmp, /var.
Bind-mount: make the source visible at a second mountpoint. mount --bind. The volume primitive every container runtime uses.
Apply operation recursively to all submounts. Combine with MS_BIND for rbind.
Set propagation type to private (no event propagation).
Set propagation type to shared (bidirectional events with peers).
Set propagation type to slave (receives from master, doesn't send).
Cannot be source of a bind-mount.
Don't update file access time on read. Common perf tweak.
Remount existing mount with new flags (e.g., remount,rw).
0 = heuristic, 1 = always allow, 2 = strict (commit ≤ overcommit_ratio% of RAM+swap). The ENOMEM-from-malloc-vs-OOM-on-touch fork.
With overcommit_memory=2, percentage of RAM that can be committed (plus all of swap).
How aggressively kernel swaps. 0 = avoid unless OOM imminent. 100 = swap freely. Servers commonly set 1-10.
1 = pagecache, 2 = dentries+inodes, 3 = both. Diagnostic tool; releases reclaimable memory.
Per-process VMA count ceiling. Elasticsearch / databases often need raised to 262144.
Maximum PID number. PIDs wrap around at this value.
System-wide thread count ceiling. Hitting it: clone() returns EAGAIN.
Max single SysV SHM segment size.
System-wide SysV SHM total in pages.
1 = require CAP_SYSLOG to read /dev/kmsg / dmesg. Container hardening.
0 = anyone with same uid; 1 = only descendants; 2 = CAP_SYS_PTRACE only; 3 = no ptrace ever (unrecoverable until reboot).
Filename template for core dumps. '|<program>' pipes to a handler — what systemd-coredump installs as '|/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-coredump %P %u %g %s %t %c %h'.
Append .PID to core dump filename. Largely superseded by %p in core_pattern.
SysRq trigger enabled features. 0 = disabled, 1 = all, otherwise bitmask. echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger reboots immediately.
System-wide max open file count.
Per-process max FDs ceiling (RLIMIT_NOFILE cannot exceed).
Per-user inotify watch count. IDEs/file watchers commonly need raised to 524288.
Per-instance inotify queue depth.
Per-user max nested user namespaces. 0 effectively disables unprivileged userns.
PID namespace identifier. Target is 'pid:[<inode>]'. setns(2) takes an FD opened on this.
User namespace identifier.
Mount namespace identifier.
Network namespace identifier.

User-namespace UID translation table. Format: 'inside_uid host_uid count' lines. Writable by privileged caller in parent namespace, OR (unprivileged) only a 1:1 mapping for the calling user unless setgroups=deny written first (and gid_map after).
User-namespace GID translation table. Companion to uid_map.
Gates setgroups(2) inside the userns. Must be 'deny' before unprivileged gid_map write.
Override the user-space init binary the kernel execs after rootfs mount.
Root filesystem device. Specifier forms: /dev/sda1, UUID=..., LABEL=..., PARTUUID=...
Mount root filesystem read-only at boot (init usually remounts rw later).
Mount root read-write at boot.
Suppress most boot messages on console.
Show graphical boot splash (plymouth integration).
Kernel printk minimum log level for console (0=emerg .. 7=debug).
Console device for kernel messages (and optionally early-userspace). e.g. console=ttyS0,115200.
Auto-reboot delay after kernel panic. 0 = never reboot.
Force kernel to use only N bytes/MB/GB of RAM (e.g. mem=4G).
Reserve memory for kdump capture kernel. e.g. crashkernel=256M.
Disable kernel address-space layout randomization. Useful for kernel debugging.
CPU vulnerability mitigations (Spectre/Meltdown family). off = max performance, no protection.
Enable Intel IOMMU (VT-d) for DMA remapping. Required for VFIO PCI passthrough.
Generic IOMMU mode. 'pt' = passthrough mode for the host kernel.
Intel P-state CPU frequency driver mode.
Disable v1 hierarchies for the listed controllers. e.g. cgroup_no_v1=all to enforce v2-only.
systemd's preference for cgroup v2 unified hierarchy. 1 = pure v2; 0 = legacy v1.
THP allocation policy. 'never' often recommended for DBs (Mongo, Redis) due to defrag latency.
Huge page size to allocate at boot (combine with hugepages=).
Number of huge pages to reserve at boot (size from hugepagesz=).
Disable IPv6 entirely at kernel level.
Enable kernel audit subsystem at boot.
Order in which LSMs initialize. Stackable LSMs evaluated in this order.
Enable/disable SELinux at boot. Combines with enforcing= for mode.
SELinux enforcing/permissive at boot.
/proc/diskstats field: number of IOs currently in progress on the device.
/proc/diskstats field: total time spent doing IOs (saturation indicator).
Total reads completed.
Reads merged before queueing (block layer optimization indicator).
Sectors read (sector = 512 bytes traditionally).
Total writes completed.
Writes merged before queueing.
Sectors written.
If set, UID 0 does NOT confer root capabilities (no auto-grant of full P set on UID 0).
If set, capability sets are NOT recalculated on UID 0↔nonzero transitions.
If set, capabilities are preserved when UID 0 changes to nonzero (vs being cleared). Same as PR_SET_KEEPCAPS.
Locks SECBIT_NOROOT — cannot be cleared after setting.
Get the ID of a special keyring (thread, process, session, user, etc.) — possibly creating it.
Replace the session keyring with a new (named or anonymous) one.
Mark a key revoked — subsequent ops on it return EKEYREVOKED.
Add a key to a keyring.
Remove a key from a keyring.
Search a keyring (and subkeyrings) for a key matching type+description.
Read the payload of a key (if read permission granted).
Whether thread is joinable (default) or starts detached.
Initial stack size for new thread. Honor RLIMIT_STACK by default.
Contention scope. SYSTEM (Linux NPTL only supports this) = compete with all system threads.
Scheduling policy for the new thread.

signal-safety(7) lists ~80 functions safe to call from a signal handler. Includes _exit, abort, accept, alarm, chdir, close, dup, execve, fork, fstat, kill, listen, lseek, open, pipe, raise, read, recv, send, setpgid, setsid, sigaction, sigprocmask, write — but NOT printf, malloc, fprintf, syslog.
malloc/free are NOT async-signal-safe (they take internal locks). Calling them from a signal handler can deadlock if the interrupted code held the same lock.
stdio (printf, fprintf, fopen) is NOT async-signal-safe — locks per-FILE. Use write(2) directly to STDERR_FILENO if you must log from a handler.
Signal handler MUST save+restore errno around any syscall that might modify it; otherwise the interrupted code sees a corrupted errno.
